newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't "open to dialogue" - Corach.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't "open to dialogue" - Corach.

text.p: Argentina's Interior Minister Carlos Corach said the government is always open to dialogue with unions, but he said will they will achieve nothing with actions such as Thursday's general strike.
"The government is always open to all issues," said Corach, quoted by the state-run Telam news agency.
"When it is necessary for the unions to make themselves heard with any request they have many other paths open to them, which make strikes unnecessary and damaging," he said.
Despite Corach's conciliatory tone, the government has said it will not be swayed by the strike against decrees to make workplace practices more flexible.
Corach added "strikes do not solve anything."

The Labor Ministry said about 31 percent of Argentine workers had joined Thursday's stoppage. But the head of the CGT labor federation Rodolfo Daer called the strike a success and said the government would be forced to listen to its protests.
The CGT called its third strike this year after President Carlos Menem lost patience with talks with the unions to hammer out a compromise over the laws, which are aimed at reducing employers' costs.
The president passed the laws by decree, provoking unions into following up a 24-hour stoppage in August against Menem's free-market policies and their successful September strike.
The government, which said it plans more labor decrees, hopes a more flexible employment market will help reduce the country's 17.3 percent jobless rate.
